{{< include /_task-metadata/f01-status.qmd >}}

<span id="f01-record"></span>

We want to describe fuel conditions under the four overstory treatments before
and after PCT, and explore what the change in standing woody vegetation can
tell us about potential additions to surface fuels. Here we'll derive the
components, examine their distributions, and compare candidate models. The saved
fits then feed [RD04 inference and display](task-rd04.qmd) and
[RT03 Results writing](task-rt03.qmd).

## Original objective and guardrails

Create publication-only fuel components that preserve the thesis analyses while
making the pre- and post-PCT data usable as distinct reference phases. During
model fitting, retain the prescribed experimental-design random-intercept
structure; record every model candidate and diagnostic; do not treat an AIC
leader as a selected model.

- Thesis notebooks, raw data, and thesis-era `.rda` objects remain unchanged.
- Pre-PCT litter and duff are separated using the Finney–Martin model-3
  forest-floor partition; post-PCT litter and duff are deliberately omitted
  because their boundary is not currently defensible.
- Woody and herbaceous vegetation are separate in both phases.
- The primary PCT contrast is matched-transect pre-PCT minus post-PCT woody
  standing vegetation - an inferred potential surface-fuel contribution, not a
  direct slash-load measurement.

## Execution and inputs {#publication-execution}

This page is the authoritative run order for F01. Review is the default;
render with `-P recompute:true` to refresh derived results using saved models,
or `-P refit:true` to replace the fits as well. Each step explains its purpose before the code and prints its result immediately afterward.
Only the calculation inside `if (recompute)` is optional; the result display runs every time.
Publication R 4.6.2, the unchanged lockfile and committed thesis exports define
the calculation environment. Each calculation overwrites its current outputs directly.

## Shared setup

First we enable automatic labels on echoed code so each calculation can be
identified from its chunk metadata without maintaining duplicate comments. This
hidden setup runs before the first displayed chunk.

```{r}
#| label: f01-setup
#| include: false

enable_chunk_labels <- function() {
  knitr::opts_hooks$set(
    echo = function(options) {
      if (isTRUE(options$echo) && !is.null(options$label)) {
        options$code <- c(
          paste0("# ", options$label),
          options$code
        )
      }
      options
    }
  )
}

enable_chunk_labels()
```

First we'll set up how this page reads inputs and saved models and runs residual
checks. The small table reports whether we're reviewing saved results,
recomputing from existing fits, or explicitly refitting them, so we can tell
which kind of run produced the page. Missing models require an explicit refit.

```{r}
#| label: f01-parameters
#| echo: true


# A refit also refreshes the results derived from the new models.
recompute <- isTRUE(params$recompute) || isTRUE(params$refit)
output_root <- "outputs"
# Keep every calculation within the publication project.
publication_paths <- function(root) {
  list(
    root = root,
    input = file.path(root, "inputs", "thesis"),
    output = file.path(root, "outputs")
  )
}

# Missing models require an explicit refit, never an automatic fit.
read_saved_model <- function(path, task) {
  if (!file.exists(path)) {
    stop(
      "Missing saved model: ",
      path,
      ". Run quarto render task-",
      tolower(task),
      ".qmd -P refit:true"
    )
  }
  model <- readRDS(path)
  # Saved glmmTMB calls can refer to a former session's local data name.
  # Predictions and residual checks should use the model's stored rows instead.
  if (inherits(model, "glmmTMB")) {
    model$call$data <- model$frame
  }
  model
}

# Simulate population-level residuals by drawing new random effects.
publication_simulate_residuals <- function(fittedModel, ...) {
  DHARMa::simulateResiduals(fittedModel, simulateREs = "unconditional", ...)
}

# Publication-only fuel-analysis configuration.
#
# Run the task pages through Quarto. Inputs are committed
# thesis exports; no thesis environment or model objects are loaded.

publication_fuel_paths <- function(publication_root) {
  common <- publication_paths(publication_root)
  output <- file.path(common$output, "fuel")
  list(
    input = file.path(common$input, "fuel-measurements.rds"),
    legacy_load_input = file.path(common$input, "fuel-deadwood-loads.rds"),
    output = output,
    data = file.path(output, "data"),
    manifests = file.path(output, "manifests")
  )
}

publication_fuel_ids <- c("site", "treatment", "corner", "azi")

data.frame(
  Mode = if (isTRUE(params$refit)) {
    "Refit models and recompute"
  } else if (recompute) {
    "Recompute from saved models"
  } else {
    "Review saved results"
  },
  Inputs = "inputs/thesis",
  Outputs = output_root
)
```

The model comparisons produce more detail than fits comfortably on one screen.
We'll use a shared table formatter so readers can sort, search, and choose fields
in the results below. Continuous estimates use consistent rounding, while AIC
uses whole numbers to keep differences between candidates visible.

```{r}
#| label: f01-table-functions
#| echo: true

# Show two significant figures, retaining trailing zeros below one and avoiding
# scientific notation. Round before formatting so large values are rounded too.
publication_number <- function(x, digits = 2L) {
  value <- trimws(formatC(
    signif(x, digits),
    format = "fg",
    digits = digits,
    flag = "#"
  ))
  value <- sub("\\.$", "", value)
  value[is.na(x)] <- NA_character_
  value
}

# Use the same controls for analytical results and CSV review tables.
# Keep the supplied order until a reader sorts, and escape data by default so
# formulas and HTML-like text remain literal. Integer counts stay exact;
# AIC uses whole numbers; other continuous columns use significant figures.
publication_table <- function(data, digits = 2L, caption = NULL) {
  if (!is.null(digits)) {
    numeric <- vapply(
      data,
      function(x) is.numeric(x) && !is.integer(x),
      logical(1)
    )
    aic <- numeric & tolower(names(data)) == "aic"
    data[aic] <- lapply(data[aic], function(x) {
      value <- formatC(round(x), format = "f", digits = 0L)
      value[is.na(x)] <- NA_character_
      value
    })
    data[numeric & !aic] <- lapply(
      data[numeric & !aic],
      publication_number,
      digits = digits
    )
  }
  DT::datatable(
    data,
    rownames = FALSE,
    escape = TRUE,
    caption = caption,
    extensions = "Buttons",
    selection = "none",
    width = "100%",
    options = list(
      dom = "B l f r t i p",
      order = list(),
      ordering = TRUE,
      searching = TRUE,
      scrollX = TRUE,
      pageLength = 10,
      lengthMenu = list(c(10, 25, 50, -1), c("10", "25", "50", "All")),
      buttons = list(list(extend = "colvis", text = "Show/hide fields"))
    )
  )
}
```

For detailed review, we also need access to the exact saved values and formulas.
This helper makes expandable CSV tables with the same controls; reading fields
as text preserves their contents alongside the rounded analytical displays.

```{r}
#| label: f01-csv-review-function
#| echo: true

# Display every saved CSV row with the same interactive controls. Read text
# literally, including formula tildes, missing-value labels and numeric strings.
render_csv_review <- function(relative, output_root = "outputs") {
  data <- read.csv(
    file.path(output_root, sub("^publication/outputs/", "", relative)),
    colClasses = "character",
    na.strings = NULL,
    check.names = FALSE,
    strip.white = FALSE,
    fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM"
  )
  name <- basename(relative)
  review <- htmltools::tags$details(
    `data-review-source` = relative,
    htmltools::tags$summary(paste(
      name,
      "-",
      nrow(data),
      "rows,",
      ncol(data),
      "columns"
    )),
    htmltools::tags$p(htmltools::tags$a(
      href = paste0("repo-files/", relative),
      "Download CSV"
    )),
    publication_table(data, caption = paste("Complete contents of", name))
  )
  # These reviews are emitted in loops and as-is chunks; carry widget
  # dependencies into knitr explicitly instead of relying on auto-printing.
  rendered <- knitr::knit_print(review)
  knitr::knit_meta_add(attr(rendered, "knit_meta"))
  cat(rendered, sep = "\n")
}
```

RD02, RD04, and the manuscript will use these same reading and display functions.
We'll save them here so those pages handle results consistently. The printed
names show which functions are available downstream.

```{r}
#| label: f01-save-helpers
#| echo: true

# Export only reusable functions, not models or datasets.
dir.create("outputs/helpers", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
shared_helpers <- list(

)

for (name in names(shared_helpers)) {
  environment(helper_environment[[name]]) <- helper_environment
}
saveRDS(as.list(helper_environment), "outputs/helpers/task-helpers.rds")

names(shared_helpers)
```

## 01 - Derive components and audit pairing

Before comparing treatments, we need fuel components that have a defensible
meaning in each measurement phase. We'll start by partitioning the pre-PCT
forest floor into litter and duff with Finney–Martin model 3. The summary below
shows the resulting loads and how often shallow-layer extrapolations needed to
be bounded at zero. We'll leave post-PCT litter and duff out because their
boundary cannot currently be identified reliably.

```{r}
#| label: f01-01-derive-components
#| echo: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false

if (recompute) {
  # Finney and Martin (1993), model 3: cumulative forest-floor mass (Mg ha^-1)
  # from the surface to depth ds_cm within a profile of total depth dp_cm.
  # The model is used only for the pre-PCT forest-floor measurements, where the
  # recorded total depth and estimated litter proportion describe the forest floor.
  # Its fitted range does not support a negative cumulative mass; the derivation
  # script records and bounds such rare shallow-layer extrapolations at zero.
  finney_martin_cumulative_load <- function(ds_cm, dp_cm) {
    result <- 6.461 * ds_cm^1.07 - 0.254 * dp_cm
    result[ds_cm == 0] <- 0
    result
  }

  publication_root <- normalizePath(getwd(), winslash = "/")
  paths_common <- publication_paths(publication_root)

  library(dplyr)
  library(readr)
  library(tidyr)

  paths <- publication_fuel_paths(publication_root)
  dir.create(paths$data, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  dir.create(paths$manifests, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

  # Typed, checksum-validated exports from the separate thesis operation.
  transects <- readRDS(paths$input)
  legacy_total_load <- readRDS(paths$legacy_load_input)
  ids <- publication_fuel_ids

  # Keep the field measurements intact for audit. Post-PCT forest-floor values
  # are retained here but deliberately receive no duff/litter load conversion.
  forest_floor_station <- transects |>
    select(phase, all_of(ids), matches("^(duff_litter|pct_litter|fbd)[12]$")) |>
    pivot_longer(
      cols = matches("^(duff_litter|pct_litter|fbd)[12]$"),
      names_to = c(".value", "station"),
      names_pattern = "(.*?)([12])$"
    ) |>
    transmute(
      phase,
      across(all_of(ids)),
      station = as.integer(station),
      total_forest_floor_depth_cm = duff_litter,
      estimated_litter_fraction = pct_litter / 100,
      estimated_litter_depth_cm = total_forest_floor_depth_cm *
        estimated_litter_fraction,
      estimated_duff_depth_cm = total_forest_floor_depth_cm -
        estimated_litter_depth_cm,
      fuel_bed_depth_cm = fbd,
      forest_floor_load_eligible = phase == "prepct"
    )

  if (
    any(
      forest_floor_station$estimated_litter_fraction < 0 |
        forest_floor_station$estimated_litter_fraction > 1,
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  ) {
    stop("Estimated litter fractions fall outside [0, 1].")
  }

  # Finney and Martin's cumulative curve partitions the pre-PCT total profile at
  # the estimated litter/duff boundary. These are model-derived loads, not direct
  # independent bulk-density measurements of the two layers.
  forest_floor_pre_station <- forest_floor_station |>
    filter(forest_floor_load_eligible) |>
    mutate(
      total_forest_floor_load_mgha = finney_martin_cumulative_load(
        total_forest_floor_depth_cm,
        total_forest_floor_depth_cm
      ),
      litter_load_mgha = finney_martin_cumulative_load(
        estimated_litter_depth_cm,
        total_forest_floor_depth_cm
      ),
      litter_load_raw_mgha = litter_load_mgha,
      litter_load_bounded_at_zero = litter_load_raw_mgha < 0,
      litter_load_mgha = pmax(litter_load_raw_mgha, 0),
      duff_load_mgha = total_forest_floor_load_mgha - litter_load_mgha
    )

  if (any(forest_floor_pre_station$duff_load_mgha < 0, na.rm = TRUE)) {
    stop(
      "Finney-Martin component calculation produced a negative duff load; inspect the input depths before proceeding."
    )
  }

  forest_floor_components <- forest_floor_pre_station |>
    select(phase, all_of(ids), station, litter_load_mgha, duff_load_mgha) |>
    pivot_longer(
      cols = ends_with("_load_mgha"),
      names_to = "component",
      values_to = "load_mgha"
    ) |>
    mutate(
      component = recode(
        component,
        litter_load_mgha = "litter",
        duff_load_mgha = "duff"
      ),
      derivation = "Finney-Martin 1993 model 3 cumulative-load partition"
    ) |>
    summarise(
      n_stations = sum(!is.na(load_mgha)),
      load_mgha = mean(load_mgha),
      derivation = first(derivation),
      .by = c(all_of(ids), "phase", "component")
    )
  saveRDS(
    forest_floor_station,
    file.path(paths$data, "forest-floor-measurements-station.rds")
  )
  saveRDS(
    forest_floor_pre_station,
    file.path(paths$data, "forest-floor-pre-components-station.rds")
  )
}

review_floor <- readRDS(
  "outputs/fuel/data/forest-floor-pre-components-station.rds"
)
publication_table(data.frame(
  Stations = nrow(review_floor),
  `Litter extrapolations bounded at zero` = sum(
    review_floor$litter_load_bounded_at_zero
  ),
  `Mean litter (Mg/ha)` = mean(review_floor$litter_load_mgha),
  `Mean duff (Mg/ha)` = mean(review_floor$duff_load_mgha),
  check.names = FALSE
))
```

We'll keep woody and herbacaceos vegetation separate, so herbaceous loads aren't
overwheled -- they have very different implications for fire. We'll convert
cover and height using the thesis bulk densities, which used values from the
firemon database manual, these should still be interpreted as operational
convenience values rather than verified representative values for our systems.
We'll average the two stations within each transect. The displayed records show
the loads and available station counts; a missing station leaves the transect
mean missing. This review reads the combined component table saved in the next
step.

```{r}
#| label: f01-01-vegetation
#| echo: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false

if (recompute) {
  # FireMon-style vegetation calculations remain separate by physiognomic class.
  vegetation_station <- transects |>
    select(
      phase,
      all_of(ids),
      matches(
        "^(live_woody|dead_woody|avg_w_ht|live_herb|dead_herb|avg_h_ht)[12]$"
      )
    ) |>
    pivot_longer(
      cols = -c(phase, all_of(ids)),
      names_to = c(".value", "station"),
      names_pattern = "(.*?)([12])$"
    ) |>
    mutate(
      woody_height_m = if_else(live_woody == 0 & dead_woody == 0, 0, avg_w_ht),
      herb_height_m = if_else(live_herb == 0 & dead_herb == 0, 0, avg_h_ht),
      woody_load_mgha = ((live_woody + dead_woody) / 100) * woody_height_m * 18,
      herb_load_mgha = ((live_herb + dead_herb) / 100) * herb_height_m * 8
    ) |>
    select(phase, all_of(ids), station, woody_load_mgha, herb_load_mgha)

  vegetation_components <- vegetation_station |>
    pivot_longer(
      cols = ends_with("_load_mgha"),
      names_to = "component",
      values_to = "load_mgha"
    ) |>
    mutate(
      component = recode(
        component,
        woody_load_mgha = "woody_vegetation",
        herb_load_mgha = "herbaceous_vegetation"
      ),
      derivation = "FireMon cover-height bulk-density calculation retained by component"
    ) |>
    summarise(
      n_stations = sum(!is.na(load_mgha)),
      load_mgha = mean(load_mgha),
      derivation = first(derivation),
      .by = c("phase", all_of(ids), "component")
    )
}

review_components <- if (recompute) {
  vegetation_components
} else {
  readRDS("outputs/fuel/data/fuel-components-transect.rds")
}
publication_table(subset(
  review_components,
  component %in% c("woody_vegetation", "herbaceous_vegetation")
))
```

Now we can bring the vegetation and forest-floor components together with the
four exported deadwood classes, whose thesis load estimates we retain, as
calculated using point intercept theory and regional parameters. The table below
is the transect-level input for the models. Post-PCT litter and duff have no
rows, and deadwood station counts are blank because those counts are not
available in the carried-forward estimates.

```{r}
#| label: f01-01-combine-components
#| echo: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false

if (recompute) {
  dead_woody_components <- legacy_total_load |>
    select(phase, all_of(ids), onehr, tenhr, hundhr, thoushr) |>
    pivot_longer(
      cols = c(onehr, tenhr, hundhr, thoushr),
      names_to = "component",
      values_to = "load_mgha"
    ) |>
    mutate(
      derivation = "Unchanged thesis-era dead-woody load carried forward from calculate_fuel_load.rda"
    )

  # Phase comes from the identifiers retained above. Restrict the exported long
  # component table to reportable component/phase combinations.
  fuel_components_transect <- bind_rows(
    forest_floor_components,
    vegetation_components,
    dead_woody_components
  ) |>
    mutate(
      component = factor(
        component,
        levels = c(
          "litter",
          "duff",
          "onehr",
          "tenhr",
          "hundhr",
          "thoushr",
          "woody_vegetation",
          "herbaceous_vegetation"
        )
      )
    ) |>
    arrange(phase, site, treatment, corner, azi, component)
  saveRDS(
    fuel_components_transect,
    file.path(paths$data, "fuel-components-transect.rds")
  )
}

publication_table(readRDS("outputs/fuel/data/fuel-components-transect.rds"))
```

To examine woody vegetation change, we need the two measurements from the same transect.
We'll match their identifiers before calculating pre-PCT minus post-PCT load.
The pairing audit shows how many records can support that comparison and whether
any are unmatched. This difference is an indicator of potential surface-fuel
contribution; the measurements do not directly quantify deposited slash.

```{r}
#| label: f01-01-pair-transects
#| echo: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false

if (recompute) {
  # Explicit pre/post joins replace the thesis-era lexical phase ordering used to
  # construct veg_diff. The primary PCT contrast is woody standing vegetation
  # reduction; it is an inferred surface-fuel contribution, not direct slash load.
  vegetation_wide <- fuel_components_transect |>
    filter(component %in% c("woody_vegetation", "herbaceous_vegetation")) |>
    select(all_of(ids), phase, component, load_mgha) |>
    pivot_wider(
      names_from = c(component, phase),
      values_from = load_mgha,
      names_sep = "_"
    )

  fuel_bed_depth_phase <- forest_floor_station |>
    summarise(
      n_fuel_bed_stations = sum(!is.na(fuel_bed_depth_cm)),
      fuel_bed_depth_cm = mean(fuel_bed_depth_cm),
      .by = c("phase", all_of(ids))
    ) |>
    pivot_wider(
      names_from = phase,
      values_from = c(fuel_bed_depth_cm, n_fuel_bed_stations),
      names_sep = "_"
    )

  fuel_paired_transect <- vegetation_wide |>
    filter(
      !is.na(woody_vegetation_prepct),
      !is.na(woody_vegetation_postpct)
    ) |>
    inner_join(fuel_bed_depth_phase, by = ids) |>
    mutate(
      woody_standing_reduction_mgha = woody_vegetation_prepct -
        woody_vegetation_postpct,
      herbaceous_vegetation_change_mgha = herbaceous_vegetation_postpct -
        herbaceous_vegetation_prepct,
      interpretation = "Woody standing-vegetation reduction is an inferred potential surface-fuel contribution; it is not a direct slash-load measurement."
    )

  pairing_qc <- bind_rows(
    transmute(
      distinct(
        filter(vegetation_wide, !is.na(woody_vegetation_prepct)),
        across(all_of(ids))
      ),
      status = "pre-PCT woody observation"
    ),
    transmute(
      distinct(
        filter(vegetation_wide, !is.na(woody_vegetation_postpct)),
        across(all_of(ids))
      ),
      status = "post-PCT woody observation"
    ),
    transmute(
      anti_join(
        distinct(
          filter(vegetation_wide, !is.na(woody_vegetation_prepct)),
          across(all_of(ids))
        ),
        distinct(
          filter(vegetation_wide, !is.na(woody_vegetation_postpct)),
          across(all_of(ids))
        ),
        by = ids
      ),
      status = "pre-PCT woody observation without post-PCT match"
    ),
    transmute(
      anti_join(
        distinct(
          filter(vegetation_wide, !is.na(woody_vegetation_postpct)),
          across(all_of(ids))
        ),
        distinct(
          filter(vegetation_wide, !is.na(woody_vegetation_prepct)),
          across(all_of(ids))
        ),
        by = ids
      ),
      status = "post-PCT woody observation without pre-PCT match"
    ),
    transmute(
      distinct(fuel_paired_transect, across(all_of(ids))),
      status = "matched woody pair"
    )
  ) |>
    count(status, name = "n_transects")
  saveRDS(
    fuel_paired_transect,
    file.path(paths$data, "fuel-paired-transect.rds")
  )
  write_csv(pairing_qc, file.path(paths$data, "fuel-pairing-qc.csv"))
}

publication_table(read.csv("outputs/fuel/data/fuel-pairing-qc.csv"))
```

These components come from different measurements and conversions, so we'll
keep their definitions together before modeling them. The dictionary below
records units, derivations, and reporting phases for both the carried-forward
deadwood and the newly separated components. It gives the figure captions and
Methods a common source for what each load represents.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-fuel-component-dictionary
#| echo: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| tbl-cap: "Publication fuel-component dictionary generated by F01."

# tbl-fuel-component-dictionary
if (recompute) {
  data_dictionary <- tibble(
    component = c(
      "litter",
      "duff",
      "onehr",
      "tenhr",
      "hundhr",
      "thoushr",
      "woody_vegetation",
      "herbaceous_vegetation",
      "woody_standing_reduction_mgha",
      "fuel_bed_depth_cm"
    ),
    unit = c(rep("Mg ha^-1", 9), "cm"),
    reporting_phase = c(
      rep("pre-PCT only", 2),
      rep("pre-PCT and post-PCT", 6),
      "matched pre/post",
      "measurement retained for protocol review"
    ),
    definition = c(
      "Model-derived upper forest-floor load using Finney-Martin cumulative model 3 and the estimated litter-depth boundary. Negative shallow-layer extrapolations are bounded at zero and retained in the station-level audit output.",
      "Model-derived lower forest-floor load: total Finney-Martin forest-floor load minus modeled litter load. Two shallow estimated litter layers were bounded at zero after the equation returned negative mass.",
      "1-hour dead and downed woody fuel load (diameter < 0.635 cm), carried forward unchanged from the thesis line-intercept calculation.",
      "10-hour dead and downed woody fuel load (diameter 0.635-2.54 cm), carried forward unchanged from the thesis line-intercept calculation.",
      "100-hour dead and downed woody fuel load (diameter 2.54-7.62 cm), carried forward unchanged from the thesis line-intercept calculation.",
      "1000-hour dead and downed woody fuel load (diameter > 7.62 cm), combining sound and rotten wood; carried forward unchanged from the thesis line-intercept calculation.",
      "FireMon-style cover-height estimate using the existing woody bulk-density constant.",
      "FireMon-style cover-height estimate using the existing herbaceous bulk-density constant.",
      "Pre-PCT minus post-PCT woody standing vegetation; inferred potential surface-fuel contribution, not direct slash load.",
      "Recorded field value; do not interpret as slash depth until protocol comparability is confirmed."
    )
  )
  write_csv(
    data_dictionary,
    file.path(paths$data, "fuel-component-data-dictionary.csv")
  )
}

dictionary <- read.csv(
  file.path(output_root, "fuel/data/fuel-component-data-dictionary.csv"),
  check.names = FALSE
)
publication_table(dictionary)
```

We'll also record which exported inputs produced these tables and how many
litter extrapolations were bounded at zero. The provenance record below lets us
trace the derived loads back to those inputs when reviewing a model or caption.

```{r}
#| label: f01-01-provenance

#| warning: false

if (recompute) {
  provenance_lines <- c(
    "input: publication/inputs/thesis/fuel-measurements.rds",

    "forest_floor_loads: pre-PCT only",
    "forest_floor_method: Finney-Martin 1993 model 3 cumulative-load partition",
    paste0(
      "litter-load-boundary-cases: ",
      sum(forest_floor_pre_station$litter_load_bounded_at_zero)
    ),

```


The dictionary and pairing audit now define the model inputs. Fuel-bed depth
remains available for protocol review, but these calculations do not turn it
into a post-PCT slash-load estimate.

## 02 - Explore component distributions

Before choosing response distributions, we'll look at how much the observed
loads vary and how often a component is absent. The summaries below give means,
spread, quantiles, zero counts, and missingness by phase, component, and treatment.
Site, block, and corner counts show the available replication. These are raw
descriptions of the transects; adjustment for the sampling hierarchy comes with
the models later.

```{r}
#| label: f01-02-explore-components
#| echo: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false

if (recompute) {
  publication_root <- normalizePath(getwd(), winslash = "/")
  paths_common <- publication_paths(publication_root)

  library(dplyr)
  library(readr)

  paths <- publication_fuel_paths(publication_root)
  components <- readRDS(file.path(paths$data, "fuel-components-transect.rds"))
  paired <- readRDS(file.path(paths$data, "fuel-paired-transect.rds"))

  add_design_groups <- function(data) {
    data |>
      mutate(
        block = interaction(site, treatment, drop = TRUE),
        design_corner = interaction(site, treatment, corner, drop = TRUE)
      )
  }

  component_data <- components |>
    mutate(component = as.character(component)) |>
    add_design_groups()

  component_summary <- component_data |>
    summarise(
      n_transects = n(),
      n_sites = n_distinct(site),
      n_blocks = n_distinct(block),
      n_corners = n_distinct(design_corner),
      n_zero = sum(load_mgha == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
      prop_zero = mean(load_mgha == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
      n_missing = sum(is.na(load_mgha)),
      mean_mgha = mean(load_mgha, na.rm = TRUE),
      sd_mgha = sd(load_mgha, na.rm = TRUE),
      variance_mgha = var(load_mgha, na.rm = TRUE),
      cv = if_else(mean_mgha > 0, sd_mgha / mean_mgha, NA_real_),
      min_mgha = min(load_mgha, na.rm = TRUE),
      q25_mgha = quantile(load_mgha, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE, names = FALSE),
      median_mgha = median(load_mgha, na.rm = TRUE),
      q75_mgha = quantile(load_mgha, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE, names = FALSE),
      max_mgha = max(load_mgha, na.rm = TRUE),
      .by = c("phase", "component", "treatment")
    ) |>
    arrange(phase, component, treatment)
  write_csv(
    component_summary,
    file.path(paths$data, "fuel-component-exploration-summary.csv")
  )
}

publication_table(read.csv(
  "outputs/fuel/data/fuel-component-exploration-summary.csv"
))
```

Observed zeros help us decide which components need a model for absence as well
as positive load. We'll translate that information and any missingness into a
table of proposed families and submodels, retaining the design random
intercepts. This table is a guide to the fitting stage; it contains no fitted
effects or model comparisons yet.

```{r}
#| label: f01-02-component-candidates
#| echo: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false

if (recompute) {
  component_candidates <- component_data |>
    summarise(
      n_zero = sum(load_mgha == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
      n_transects = n(),
      n_missing = sum(is.na(load_mgha)),
      .by = c("phase", "component")
    ) |>
    mutate(
      response_type = "nonnegative continuous load",
      fixed_effects = "treatment",
      random_effects = "(1 | site) + (1 | site:treatment) + (1 | site:treatment:corner)",
      conditional_family = if_else(
        n_zero > 0,
        "ziGamma(link = log)",
        "Gamma(link = log)"
      ),
      zero_inflation_candidates = if_else(
        n_zero > 0,
        "~1; consider ~treatment only if zero-process diagnostics and replication support it",
        "none unless later diagnostics identify a structural-zero process"
      ),
      dispersion_candidates = "~1 first; compare ~treatment only if residual dispersion diagnostics support it",
      status = if_else(
        n_missing > 0,
        "candidate specifications only; resolve missing values before model fitting",
        "candidate specifications only; no model fitted"
      )
    ) |>
    arrange(phase, component)
  write_csv(
    component_candidates,
    file.path(paths$manifests, "fuel-component-model-candidates.csv")
  )
}

publication_table(read.csv(
  "outputs/fuel/manifests/fuel-component-model-candidates.csv"
))
```

The paired woody differences need a separate look because subtracting two
nonnegative loads can give either sign. We'll summarize them by treatment,
including counts of reductions, increases, and unchanged loads. Their range and
spread help us judge candidate distributions for change; a Gamma response cannot
accommodate negative or zero differences.

```{r}
#| label: f01-02-paired-summary
#| echo: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false

if (recompute) {
  paired_data <- paired |>
    add_design_groups()

  paired_summary <- paired_data |>
    summarise(
      n_pairs = n(),
      n_sites = n_distinct(site),
      n_blocks = n_distinct(block),
      n_corners = n_distinct(design_corner),
      n_negative = sum(woody_standing_reduction_mgha < 0, na.rm = TRUE),
      n_zero = sum(woody_standing_reduction_mgha == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
      n_positive = sum(woody_standing_reduction_mgha > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
      mean_mgha = mean(woody_standing_reduction_mgha, na.rm = TRUE),
      sd_mgha = sd(woody_standing_reduction_mgha, na.rm = TRUE),
      min_mgha = min(woody_standing_reduction_mgha, na.rm = TRUE),
      median_mgha = median(woody_standing_reduction_mgha, na.rm = TRUE),
      max_mgha = max(woody_standing_reduction_mgha, na.rm = TRUE),
      .by = treatment
    ) |>
    arrange(treatment)
  write_csv(
    paired_summary,
    file.path(paths$data, "woody-pct-contrast-exploration-summary.csv")
  )
}

publication_table(read.csv(
  "outputs/fuel/data/woody-pct-contrast-exploration-summary.csv"
))
```

We'll capture those requirements for the change model before fitting it. The
table below keeps the signed response, treatment comparison, and design
clustering explicit. A zero difference means equal pre- and post-PCT loads, so it
does not have the same interpretation as absent vegetation in a phase-load model.

```{r}
#| label: f01-02-paired-candidate
#| echo: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false

if (recompute) {
  paired_candidate <- tibble(
    response = "woody_standing_reduction_mgha",
    response_type = "signed matched pre-PCT minus post-PCT contrast",
    fixed_effects = "treatment",
    random_effects = "(1 | site) + (1 | site:treatment) + (1 | site:treatment:corner)",
    conditional_family = "Do not use Gamma automatically; select a signed-response model after distribution diagnostics.",
    zero_inflation_candidates = "Not applicable to a signed contrast without a separate two-part estimand.",
    dispersion_candidates = "Assess residual dispersion after selecting a signed-response family.",
    status = "candidate specification only; no model fitted"
  )
  write_csv(
    paired_candidate,
    file.path(paths$manifests, "woody-pct-contrast-model-candidate.csv")
  )
}

publication_table(read.csv(
  "outputs/fuel/manifests/woody-pct-contrast-model-candidate.csv"

```


These summaries give us a starting point for the candidate distributions.
Whether the models describe the observed variation adequately still needs to
be checked against their residuals.

## Fitting and residual-check functions

To compare candidates fairly, we'll define `fit_and_diagnose()` to give each one
the same fitting record and residual checks. When called, it reads the candidate's
saved model through `read_saved_model()` unless `refit:true` explicitly requests
the optimizer and saves a replacement fit. It retains warnings and convergence
information and adds simulation-based diagnostics, returning one register row
per attempt. Those fields help us distinguish a promising AIC from a fit that
still needs work. Sections 03 and 04 call this function during recompute or refit;
an ordinary review render reads their saved registers instead.

Small label helpers describe formulas and family objects directly, so each
candidate only needs to specify its model components. The optional
`family_label`, `ziformula_label`, and `dispformula_label` arguments can still
supply display text. In particular, `ziGamma()` identifies itself as `"Gamma"`
inside its family object, so we keep its explicit label to distinguish that
constructor. We also retain the Gaussian and Student-t display names.

```{r}
#| label: f01-fit-and-diagnose
#| echo: true

# Create and return the model and diagnostic output folders.
model_output_paths <- function(paths) {
  models <- file.path(paths$output, "models")
  diagnostics <- file.path(paths$output, "diagnostics")
  dir.create(models, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  dir.create(diagnostics, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  list(models = models, diagnostics = diagnostics)
}

# Extract test results, retaining errors so other checks can continue.
extract_test <- function(test_fun, simulation) {
  result <- tryCatch(test_fun(simulation), error = function(error) error)
  if (inherits(result, "error")) {
    return(list(
      statistic = NA_real_,
      p_value = NA_real_,
      error = conditionMessage(result)
    ))
  }
  list(
    statistic = unname(result$statistic)[1],
    p_value = result$p.value,
    error = NA_character_
  )
}

# Keep formulas on one line, preserving operators and quoted variable names.
default_formula_label <- function(formula, label = NULL) {
  if (!is.null(label)) return(label)
  paste(trimws(deparse(formula, width.cutoff = 500L)), collapse = " ")
}

# Use family metadata rather than the expression or variable passed by a caller.
default_family_label <- function(family, label = NULL) {
  if (!is.null(label)) return(label)
  paste0(family$family, "(link = ", family$link, ")")
}

fit_and_diagnose <- function(
  model_id,
  response,
  analysis,
  data,
  formula,
  family,
  ziformula,
  dispformula,
  paths,
  simulation_n,
  simulation_seed,
  family_label = NULL,
  ziformula_label = NULL,
  dispformula_label = NULL
) {
  output_paths <- model_output_paths(paths)
  warnings <- character()
  fit <- if (isTRUE(params$refit)) {
    tryCatch(
      withCallingHandlers(
        glmmTMB::glmmTMB(
          formula = formula,
          data = data,
          family = family,
          ziformula = ziformula,
          dispformula = dispformula
        ),
        warning = function(warning) {
          warnings <<- c(warnings, conditionMessage(warning))
          invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
        }
      ),
      error = function(error) error
    )
  } else {
    read_saved_model(
      file.path(output_paths$models, paste0(model_id, ".rds")),
      "F01"
    )
  }

  # Fitting warnings are saved evidence; refreshing residuals must retain them.
  if (!isTRUE(params$refit)) {
    saved_register <- read.csv(file.path(
      paths$manifests,
      "model-comparison.csv"
    ))
    warnings <- stats::na.omit(saved_register$warnings[
      saved_register$model_id == model_id
    ])
  }

  base_record <- tibble::tibble(
    model_id = model_id,
    response = response,
    analysis = analysis,
    n = nrow(data),
    fixed_and_random_formula = default_formula_label(formula),
    family = default_family_label(family, family_label),
    ziformula = default_formula_label(ziformula, ziformula_label),
    dispformula = default_formula_label(dispformula, dispformula_label),
    fit_status = if (inherits(fit, "error")) "error" else "fit",
    fit_message = if (inherits(fit, "error")) {
      conditionMessage(fit)
    } else {
      NA_character_
    },
    warnings = if (length(warnings)) {
      paste(unique(warnings), collapse = " | ")
    } else {
      NA_character_
    },
    pd_hessian = NA,
    aic = NA_real_,
    dharma_uniformity_p = NA_real_,
    dharma_dispersion_p = NA_real_,
    dharma_outlier_p = NA_real_,
    dharma_zero_inflation_p = NA_real_,
    diagnostic_message = NA_character_
  )

  if (inherits(fit, "error")) {
    return(base_record)
  }

  if (isTRUE(params$refit)) {
    saveRDS(fit, file.path(output_paths$models, paste0(model_id, ".rds")))
  }
  simulation <- tryCatch(
    publication_simulate_residuals(
      fit,
      n = simulation_n,
      seed = simulation_seed
    ),
    error = function(error) error
  )
  if (inherits(simulation, "error")) {
    return(dplyr::mutate(
      base_record,
      pd_hessian = fit$sdr$pdHess,
      aic = stats::AIC(fit),
      diagnostic_message = conditionMessage(simulation)
    ))
  }

  # Some DHARMa tests may draw internally. Use a null device so these
  # exploratory diagnostics never create an incidental Rplots.pdf in analysis/.
  grDevices::pdf(file = NULL)
  on.exit(grDevices::dev.off(), add = TRUE)
  uniformity <- extract_test(DHARMa::testUniformity, simulation)
  dispersion <- extract_test(DHARMa::testDispersion, simulation)
  outliers <- extract_test(DHARMa::testOutliers, simulation)
  zero_inflation <- extract_test(DHARMa::testZeroInflation, simulation)

  png(
    filename = file.path(
      output_paths$diagnostics,
      paste0(model_id, "-dharma.png")
    ),
    width = 1800,
    height = 900,
    res = 150
  )
  plot(simulation)
  dev.off()

  dplyr::mutate(
    base_record,
    pd_hessian = fit$sdr$pdHess,
    aic = stats::AIC(fit),
    dharma_uniformity_p = uniformity$p_value,
    dharma_dispersion_p = dispersion$p_value,
    dharma_outlier_p = outliers$p_value,
    dharma_zero_inflation_p = zero_inflation$p_value,
    diagnostic_message = paste(
      stats::na.omit(c(
        uniformity$error,
        dispersion$error,
        outliers$error,
        zero_inflation$error
      )),
      collapse = " | "
    )
  )
}
```

## 03 - Fit phase-component candidates

We'll now ask whether treatment differences in each component can be described
with a common residual dispersion, or whether dispersion also needs to vary by
treatment. Positive loads use Gamma models with a log link; components with
zeros also get a zero submodel, with treatment-specific zero probabilities
considered when there are at least eight zeros. The code defines these
candidates and retains the additional site and dispersion alternatives for
post-PCT 100-hour fuel.

```{r}
#| label: f01-03-fit-phase-components
#| echo: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false

if (recompute) {
  # Preserve the fresh-Rscript RNG boundary of this historical fitting stage.
  # DHARMa 0.5.0 consumes an extra draw when .Random.seed is initially absent.
  if (exists(".Random.seed", envir = .GlobalEnv, inherits = FALSE)) {
    rm(".Random.seed", envir = .GlobalEnv)
  }
  publication_root <- normalizePath(getwd(), winslash = "/")
  paths_common <- publication_paths(publication_root)

  # Reuse the fitting functions defined above.

  library(dplyr)
  library(purrr)
  library(readr)

  paths <- publication_fuel_paths(publication_root)
  output_paths <- model_output_paths(paths)
  components <- readRDS(file.path(
    paths$data,
    "fuel-components-transect.rds"
  )) |>
    mutate(
      component = as.character(component),
      block = interaction(site, treatment, drop = TRUE),
      design_corner = interaction(site, treatment, corner, drop = TRUE)
    )

  design_formula <- load_mgha ~ treatment +
    (1 | site) +
    (1 | block) +
    (1 | design_corner)

  fit_component_candidates <- function(data, phase_value, component_value) {
    model_data <- data |>
      filter(
        .data$phase == .env$phase_value,
        .data$component == .env$component_value,
        !is.na(load_mgha)
      )
    zero_count <- sum(model_data$load_mgha == 0)
    prefix <- paste(phase_value, component_value, sep = "_")

    candidates <- list()
    if (zero_count > 0) {
      candidates[["base"]] <- list(
        family = glmmTMB::ziGamma(link = "log"),
        family_label = "ziGamma(link = log)",
        ziformula = ~1,
        dispformula = ~1
      )
      candidates[["disp_treatment"]] <- list(
        family = glmmTMB::ziGamma(link = "log"),
        family_label = "ziGamma(link = log)",
        ziformula = ~1,
        dispformula = ~treatment
      )
      if (zero_count >= 8) {
        candidates[["zi_treatment"]] <- list(
          family = glmmTMB::ziGamma(link = "log"),
          family_label = "ziGamma(link = log)",
          ziformula = ~treatment,
          dispformula = ~1
        )
      }
    } else {
      candidates[["base"]] <- list(
        family = Gamma(link = "log"),
        ziformula = ~0,
        dispformula = ~1
      )
      candidates[["disp_treatment"]] <- list(
        family = Gamma(link = "log"),
        ziformula = ~0,
        dispformula = ~treatment
      )
    }

    # The thesis used site plus treatment in both the zero and dispersion
    # submodels for post-PCT 100-hour fuels. Retain that candidate and add one
    # deliberately more complex site-by-treatment dispersion sensitivity check.
    if (phase_value == "postpct" && component_value == "hundhr") {
      candidates[["zi_treatment_site_disp_treatment_site"]] <- list(
        family = glmmTMB::ziGamma(link = "log"),
        family_label = "ziGamma(link = log)",
        ziformula = ~ treatment + site,
        dispformula = ~ treatment + site
      )
      candidates[["zi_treatment_site_disp_treatment_site_interaction"]] <- list(
        family = glmmTMB::ziGamma(link = "log"),
        family_label = "ziGamma(link = log)",
        ziformula = ~ treatment + site,
        dispformula = ~ treatment * site
      )
    }

    imap_dfr(candidates, function(candidate, candidate_name) {
      fit_and_diagnose(
        simulation_n = 1000,
        simulation_seed = 20260918,
        model_id = paste(prefix, candidate_name, sep = "_"),
        response = component_value,
        analysis = paste(phase_value, "phase-specific component", sep = ": "),
        data = model_data,
        formula = design_formula,
        family = candidate$family,
        family_label = candidate$family_label,
        ziformula = candidate$ziformula,
        dispformula = candidate$dispformula,
        paths = paths
      )
    })
  }
}
```

We'll apply those candidates to each component–phase dataset and collect every
attempt in the register below. Convergence fields and DHARMa tests, based on
1,000 unconditional simulations with seed 20260918, help identify fits needing
follow-up before we use their treatment estimates.

```{r}
#| label: f01-03-fit-register
#| echo: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false

if (recompute) {
  registry <- components |>
    distinct(phase, component) |>
    arrange(phase, component) |>
    pmap_dfr(function(phase, component) {
      fit_component_candidates(components, phase, component)
    })

  write_csv(
    registry,
    file.path(paths$manifests, "phase-component-model-registry.csv")
  )
}

publication_table(read.csv(
  "outputs/fuel/manifests/phase-component-model-registry.csv"
))
```


The register keeps convergence problems and residual flags alongside the
candidate results. We'll carry those concerns into model review even when a
candidate has the lowest AIC.

## 04 - Fit matched woody candidates

Without a defensible post-PCT slash-depth conversion, the change in standing
woody load offers one way to explore PCT's potential contribution to surface
fuels. We'll compare a model of the paired differences with a joint model of
the two phases. Woody loads are nonnegative, include zeros,
and can be strongly right-skewed. A difference between two such loads can be
negative, zero, or positive, with a distribution unlike either phase alone.
Modeling the loads jointly respects their original scale and supplies both
phase estimates. Modeling the observed differences directly asks whether a
simpler change response gives a defensible account of the same paired data.
These alternatives test different distributional and variance assumptions;
they do not change the definition of woody reduction.

For transect $i$, the observed signed difference is
$d_i = y_{i,\mathrm{pre}} - y_{i,\mathrm{post}}$. Positive values indicate less
standing woody vegetation after PCT; negative values indicate more. Here,
"signed-difference model" means fitting $d_i$ directly, while "contrast from
the joint phase model" means subtracting its two fitted response-scale means.
Both yield signed changes in Mg/ha; a contrast is a derived quantity, not a
separate response family.

| Feature | Joint phase model and derived contrast | Direct signed-difference model |
|---|---|---|
| Response | Two woody loads per matched transect, one per phase. | One observed pre-minus-post difference per matched transect. |
| Treatment effects | `phase * treatment` allows phase change to vary by treatment. | `treatment` allows the difference to vary by treatment. |
| Distribution | A zero probability plus a Gamma distribution for positive loads, with a log link. | Gaussian or Student-t with an identity link, allowing either sign. |
| Pairing and design | Site, block, and corner random intercepts, plus a shared transect intercept linking the two phases. | Pairing is already used in the subtraction; site, block, and corner random intercepts retain clustering among differences. |
| Available estimates | Pre- and post-PCT mean loads and their covariance-aware difference. | Treatment-specific differences; the two phase means cannot be recovered from differences alone. |

For the joint model, RD04 derives
$\Delta_t = \mu_{\mathrm{pre},t} - \mu_{\mathrm{post},t}$ from means that include
the zero probability and integrate over the fitted random effects, with equal
study-site weights. Exponentiating a phase contrast on the log scale would
instead give a ratio in the positive-load submodel. The uncertainty of the
response-scale difference retains the covariance between the estimated phase
means: $\operatorname{Var}(\hat\Delta_t) =
\operatorname{Var}(\hat\mu_{\mathrm{pre},t}) +
\operatorname{Var}(\hat\mu_{\mathrm{post},t}) -
2\operatorname{Cov}(\hat\mu_{\mathrm{pre},t},\hat\mu_{\mathrm{post},t})$.
The direct model represents paired change through the distribution of $d_i$
itself. Although $E(Y_{\mathrm{pre}}-Y_{\mathrm{post}}) =
E(Y_{\mathrm{pre}})-E(Y_{\mathrm{post}})$ when the means exist, separately fitted
models need not give identical estimates or intervals because their assumptions
and use of the phase information differ.

The three joint candidates use a common zero
probability and dispersion, a phase-specific zero probability, or phase-specific
dispersion. These distinguish changes in the frequency of absent woody
vegetation from changes in the spread of positive loads. The six direct
candidates use Gaussian errors with common or treatment-specific dispersion,
or Student-t errors with common, treatment, additive treatment-plus-site, or
treatment-by-site dispersion. Student-t provides heavier tails for unusually
large changes; the dispersion alternatives assess whether residual spread
differs among treatments and sites. No zero-inflation submodel is used for the
signed response: a zero difference means equal phase loads, not necessarily
absent woody vegetation. The family and submodel definitions follow the
[glmmTMB family documentation](https://glmmtmb.github.io/glmmTMB/reference/nbinom2.html)
and [fitting documentation](https://glmmtmb.github.io/glmmTMB/reference/glmmTMB.html).

The current saved fits use 234 phase-load observations or 117 paired differences.
Their likelihoods describe different responses, so AIC is compared **within**
each approach, not across the two approaches, following the
[same-data requirement for AIC](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/stats/html/AIC.html).
Convergence and residual checks still determine what needs follow-up. RD04 uses
the joint model so its displayed woody change agrees with its phase means;
the direct models remain sensitivity candidates. Neither approach establishes
a causal PCT effect or measures slash production directly.

The cell below fits both candidate sets and brings all nine attempts into one
register. We'll use its convergence and residual fields to assess the alternatives
alongside AIC within each approach. Diagnostics use 1,000 unconditional DHARMa
simulations with seed 20260918; recompute reads saved models, refit replaces
them, and an ordinary render shows the saved register.

```{r}
#| label: f01-04-fit-woody-pct-models
#| echo: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false

if (recompute) {
  # This stage formerly started in a separate Rscript process. Restore its empty
  # initial RNG state; the diagnostic seed and unconditional simulations are unchanged.
  if (exists(".Random.seed", envir = .GlobalEnv, inherits = FALSE)) {
    rm(".Random.seed", envir = .GlobalEnv)
  }
  publication_root <- normalizePath(getwd(), winslash = "/")
  paths_common <- publication_paths(publication_root)

  # Reuse the fitting functions defined above.

  library(dplyr)
  library(readr)
  library(tidyr)

  paths <- publication_fuel_paths(publication_root)
  output_paths <- model_output_paths(paths)
  paired <- readRDS(file.path(paths$data, "fuel-paired-transect.rds")) |>
    mutate(
      block = interaction(site, treatment, drop = TRUE),
      design_corner = interaction(site, treatment, corner, drop = TRUE),
      transect_id = interaction(site, treatment, corner, azi, drop = TRUE)
    )

  woody_long <- paired |>
    select(
      site,
      treatment,
      corner,
      azi,
      block,
      design_corner,
      transect_id,
      woody_vegetation_prepct,
      woody_vegetation_postpct
    ) |>
    pivot_longer(
      cols = starts_with("woody_vegetation_"),
      names_to = "phase",
      names_prefix = "woody_vegetation_",
      values_to = "load_mgha"
    ) |>
    mutate(phase = factor(phase, levels = c("prepct", "postpct")))

  phase_formula <- load_mgha ~ phase *
    treatment +
    (1 | site) +
    (1 | block) +
    (1 | design_corner) +
    (1 | transect_id)

  # Model the paired phase loads; RD04 derives their response-scale contrast.
  phase_registry <- bind_rows(
    fit_and_diagnose(
      simulation_n = 1000,
      simulation_seed = 20260918,
      model_id = "woody_phase_zigamma_zi1_disp1",
      response = "woody vegetation load",
      analysis = "matched repeated-measures phase model",
      data = woody_long,
      formula = phase_formula,
      family = glmmTMB::ziGamma(link = "log"),
      family_label = "ziGamma(link = log)",
      ziformula = ~1,
      dispformula = ~1,
      paths = paths
    ),
    fit_and_diagnose(
      simulation_n = 1000,
      simulation_seed = 20260918,
      model_id = "woody_phase_zigamma_ziphase_disp1",
      response = "woody vegetation load",
      analysis = "matched repeated-measures phase model",
      data = woody_long,
      formula = phase_formula,
      family = glmmTMB::ziGamma(link = "log"),
      family_label = "ziGamma(link = log)",
      ziformula = ~phase,
      dispformula = ~1,
      paths = paths
    ),
    fit_and_diagnose(
      simulation_n = 1000,
      simulation_seed = 20260918,
      model_id = "woody_phase_zigamma_zi1_dispphase",
      response = "woody vegetation load",
      analysis = "matched repeated-measures phase model",
      data = woody_long,
      formula = phase_formula,
      family = glmmTMB::ziGamma(link = "log"),
      family_label = "ziGamma(link = log)",
      ziformula = ~1,
      dispformula = ~phase,
      paths = paths
    )
  )

  # Model each transect's observed signed difference directly.
  delta_formula <- woody_standing_reduction_mgha ~ treatment +
    (1 | site) +
    (1 | block) +
    (1 | design_corner)

  delta_registry <- bind_rows(
    fit_and_diagnose(
      simulation_n = 1000,
      simulation_seed = 20260918,
      model_id = "woody_delta_gaussian",
      response = "woody standing-vegetation reduction",
      analysis = "signed matched pre-minus-post contrast",
      data = paired,
      formula = delta_formula,
      family = gaussian(),
      family_label = "Gaussian(identity)",
      ziformula = ~0,
      dispformula = ~1,
      paths = paths
    ),
    fit_and_diagnose(
      simulation_n = 1000,
      simulation_seed = 20260918,
      model_id = "woody_delta_gaussian_disp_treatment",
      response = "woody standing-vegetation reduction",
      analysis = "signed matched pre-minus-post contrast",
      data = paired,
      formula = delta_formula,
      family = gaussian(),
      family_label = "Gaussian(identity)",
      ziformula = ~0,
      dispformula = ~treatment,
      paths = paths
    ),
    fit_and_diagnose(
      simulation_n = 1000,
      simulation_seed = 20260918,
      model_id = "woody_delta_student_t",
      response = "woody standing-vegetation reduction",
      analysis = "signed matched pre-minus-post contrast",
      data = paired,
      formula = delta_formula,
      family = glmmTMB::t_family(),
      family_label = "Student-t(identity)",
      ziformula = ~0,
      dispformula = ~1,
      paths = paths
    ),
    fit_and_diagnose(
      simulation_n = 1000,
      simulation_seed = 20260918,
      model_id = "woody_delta_student_t_disp_treatment",
      response = "woody standing-vegetation reduction",
      analysis = "signed matched pre-minus-post contrast",
      data = paired,
      formula = delta_formula,
      family = glmmTMB::t_family(),
      family_label = "Student-t(identity)",
      ziformula = ~0,
      dispformula = ~treatment,
      paths = paths
    ),
    fit_and_diagnose(
      simulation_n = 1000,
      simulation_seed = 20260918,
      model_id = "woody_delta_student_t_disp_treatment_site",
      response = "woody standing-vegetation reduction",
      analysis = "signed matched pre-minus-post contrast",
      data = paired,
      formula = delta_formula,
      family = glmmTMB::t_family(),
      family_label = "Student-t(identity)",
      ziformula = ~0,
      dispformula = ~ treatment + site,
      paths = paths
    ),
    fit_and_diagnose(
      simulation_n = 1000,
      simulation_seed = 20260918,
      model_id = "woody_delta_student_t_disp_treatment_site_interaction",
      response = "woody standing-vegetation reduction",
      analysis = "signed matched pre-minus-post contrast",
      data = paired,
      formula = delta_formula,
      family = glmmTMB::t_family(),
      family_label = "Student-t(identity)",
      ziformula = ~0,
      dispformula = ~ treatment * site,
      paths = paths
    )
  )

  write_csv(
    bind_rows(phase_registry, delta_registry),
    file.path(paths$manifests, "woody-pct-model-registry.csv")
  )
}

review_woody <- read.csv("outputs/fuel/manifests/woody-pct-model-registry.csv")
publication_table(review_woody)
```


For the current display, RD04 uses the joint phase model so the woody change
agrees with its phase means and retains their covariance. The direct-difference
fits remain available for sensitivity review.

## 05 - Evaluate provisional model leaders

With the candidate fits assembled, we can ask which has the strongest relative
support within each response and analysis group. The comparison below ranks AIC
and shows the distance from the leader while retaining convergence and residual
evidence. These rankings narrow the review; they do not settle whether the
model assumptions are suitable for the study question.

```{r}
#| label: f01-05-evaluate-and-select-models
#| echo: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false

if (recompute) {
  publication_root <- normalizePath(getwd(), winslash = "/")
  paths_common <- publication_paths(publication_root)

  library(dplyr)
  library(readr)

  paths <- publication_fuel_paths(publication_root)
  registry_files <- c(
    file.path(paths$manifests, "phase-component-model-registry.csv"),
    file.path(paths$manifests, "woody-pct-model-registry.csv")
  )
  if (!all(file.exists(registry_files))) {
    stop(
      "F01 model registers are missing. Run quarto render task-f01.qmd -P refit:true."
    )
  }

  registry <- bind_rows(lapply(
    registry_files,
    read_csv,
    show_col_types = FALSE
  )) |>
    mutate(
      comparison_group = paste(response, analysis, sep = " | ")
    ) |>
    mutate(
      aic_rank = if_else(
        fit_status == "fit",
        rank(aic, ties.method = "min"),
        NA_real_
      ),
      delta_aic = if_else(
        fit_status == "fit",
        aic - min(aic[fit_status == "fit"], na.rm = TRUE),
        NA_real_
      ),
      .by = comparison_group
    ) |>
    arrange(comparison_group, aic_rank, model_id)
  write_csv(registry, file.path(paths$manifests, "model-comparison.csv"))
}

publication_table(read.csv("outputs/fuel/manifests/model-comparison.csv"))
```

### Provisional model-review register {#rendered-provisional-model-review-register}

We'll pull the AIC leaders into a shorter review register so unresolved
convergence or residual problems are easy to find. Its status column identifies
what needs follow-up before scientific acceptance and gives RD04 a record to
consult when drafting the fuel display.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-fuel-provisional-models
#| echo: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| tbl-cap: "Provisional AIC-leading fuel models generated by F01; these are not final selections."

# tbl-fuel-provisional-models
if (recompute) {
  selection_log <- registry |>
    filter(fit_status == "fit", aic_rank == 1) |>
    mutate(
      diagnostic_follow_up = rowSums(
        across(starts_with("dharma_"), ~ !is.na(.x) & .x < 0.05)
      ) >
        0
    ) |>
    transmute(
      response,
      analysis,
      provisional_aic_leader = model_id,
      aic,
      pd_hessian,
      dharma_uniformity_p,
      dharma_dispersion_p,
      dharma_outlier_p,
      dharma_zero_inflation_p,
      selection_status = case_when(
        !pd_hessian ~ "rejected pending convergence resolution",
        diagnostic_follow_up ~ "requires diagnostic follow-up",
        TRUE ~ "eligible for scientific review"
      ),
      selection_rationale = "This is the AIC-leading predeclared candidate, not a final selection. Retain only after diagnostic and scientific review."
    )

  write_csv(
    selection_log,
    file.path(paths$manifests, "model-selection-log.csv")
  )
}

leaders <- read.csv(
  file.path(output_root, "fuel/manifests/model-selection-log.csv"),
  check.names = FALSE
)
leaders <- leaders[, c(
  "response",
  "analysis",
  "provisional_aic_leader",
  "pd_hessian",
  "dharma_uniformity_p",
  "dharma_dispersion_p",
  "selection_status"
)]
names(leaders) <- c(
  "Response",
  "Analysis",
  "Provisional leader",
  "PD Hessian",
  "DHARMa uniformity p",
  "DHARMa dispersion p",
  "Status"
)
publication_table(leaders)
```


We've separated the fuel components, checked the pre- and post-PCT pairing,
and fitted and compared candidate models for the phase-specific loads and woody
vegetation change. Most matched transects had less standing woody vegetation
after PCT, giving us an indicator of its potential contribution to surface fuels;
we still cannot translate that reduction directly into a measured slash load.
The component definitions also keep litter and duff estimates confined to the
pre-PCT phase, where their separation is defensible. Both the direct-difference
and joint-phase approaches now have saved fits and diagnostics, with AIC leaders
that remain provisional pending scientific review. These results give
[RD04](task-rd04.qmd) a basis for estimating and displaying fuel loads and the
woody phase contrast, while retaining the alternative fits for sensitivity
review and keeping the interpretation clear for the publication's fuel Results.
